v1.feedback: The IFS fern-to-shedding arc is a strong embodiment of mono no aware — growth, breeze, then tip-first leaf-fall while the bare rachis persists is genuinely poetic. Palette is excellent (umber→rust→amber→bone, all low-saturation earth tones). Two refinements: the shedding wobble frequencies (5.0, 3.7) and lateral drift distances (up to 3.0 units) risk making the fall feel busy rather than contemplative — halve those wobble speeds and cap lateral scatter at ~1.5 to get the slow, resigned drift of actual autumn leaves. Second, the fallen-leaf ground carpet (groundY = -0.3 + random*0.5) is very thin; spreading it slightly and fading alpha further on landed particles would sell the 'carpet of spent leaves' image and give the bare stem more visual solitude.

v2.feedback: Strong conceptual mapping — the tip-first shedding with per-particle autumn color transition genuinely embodies mono no aware rather than just illustrating it. Ensure OrbitControls.autoRotate is explicitly false in the truncated setup code; if orbit damping is present, set it high (0.92+) so user drags feel weighty. The fallen carpet could benefit from a very slight alpha fade over time (leaves decomposing) to complete the transience cycle and prevent the ground from becoming visually heavier than the still-standing rachis.
